question: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?
explanation: The left ventricle has a thick muscular wall designed to pump blood through the aorta to the rest of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle thicker than the right ventricle?

options.A: It holds a larger volume of blood
options.B: It gets blood directly from the lungs under high pressure
options.C: It pumps blood through the whole body against high pressure
options.D: It beats much faster than the right side

explanation: Think of it this way: the left side has to push blood all the way to your toes and fingers, while the right side only goes to the nearby lungs. More distance means it needs more muscle power!

question: What is the main job of the chordae tendineae in the heart?

options.A: Carrying oxygen to the heart muscle
options.B: Creating the electrical spark for each heartbeat
options.C: Stopping the AV valves from flipping backward
options.D: Opening the valves when pressure rises

explanation: You can picture these like strong little parachute cords. They hold the valve flaps tightly in place so the heavy squeezing of the heart doesn't push them inside out!

question: A patient has a leaky mitral valve. Where will blood wrongly flow when the ventricles squeeze?
explanation: Since the mitral valve sits right between the left upper and lower chambers (atrium and ventricle), a weak seal lets blood slip backward upstairs instead of going forward into the body.

question: What physical movement inside the heart makes the first heart sound (the 'lub')?

options.B: Blood rushing into the main veins

explanation: That familiar 'lub-dub' sound is actually just doors shutting! The first sound is the AV valves snapping closed so blood doesn't flow backward.

question: What is happening inside the heart during ventricular diastole?

options.A: The ventricles are forcefully pumping blood out
options.B: The ventricles are relaxing and filling with blood
options.C: The heart muscle is pulling tight
options.D: The valves are forced open by rising pressure

explanation: Remember: diastole means downtime and filling up, while systole means squeezing and pumping out. Great nursing concept to master early!

question: Which structure is known as the natural pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial node sets the normal pace for the heart because it depolarizes faster than any other conducting tissue. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why does the electrical signal take a short pause at the AV node?

options.A: To stop signals from going backward into the lungs
options.B: To slow down the heart rate during sleep
options.C: To give the SA node time to rest
options.D: To let the ventricles fill up completely with blood first

explanation: That tiny pause is super smart design! It ensures the top chambers finish emptying their blood down into the bottom chambers before the bottom chambers squeeze.

question: On an ECG machine, what does the QRS complex show us?

options.D: Lower chambers electrical activity before they squeeze

explanation: The big tall spike on the ECG screen (the QRS) is the electrical wave racing through the ventricles right before they pump blood out.

question: Which part of a normal ECG tracing shows the electrical recovery of the ventricles?
explanation: The T wave is like the heart taking a deep breath and resetting its electrical charge after a hard squeeze, getting ready for the next beat.

question: Where do the coronary arteries get their blood supply from?

options.A: The main upper vein (superior vena cava)

explanation: The heart muscle works non-stop and needs its own fuel supply! It takes the very first branches right off the aorta where the oxygen-rich blood leaves the heart.

question: What is the medical term when heart muscle cells suffer from a temporary lack of blood flow and oxygen?
explanation: Ischemia simply means a tissue is crying out because it's starved of proper blood flow. Catching it early in clinical practice saves heart muscle!
